notes: RESULT: all 22 primary anomaly files REMAIN UNINDEXED after --full-scan (all 22 token greps zero hits; 3 sampled id: lookups all return 0; comm -23 diff after remediation lists exactly the same 22 paths, no more no less). Only the 5 secondary staleness files cleared (count 65253->65258, +5; diff went from 27 missing to 22 missing). Per plan Rollback/Contingency, this is a documented possible outcome: 'If any of the 22 remain unindexed after --full-scan, stop and follow Rollback/Contingency (record outcome, recommend Xapian-level follow-up) rather than attempting deeper surgery inline.' No further inline remediation attempted. MAIL-FILE INTEGRITY: on-disk Logos file count unchanged (340 before, 340 after); all 22 target files verified byte-identical via sha256 (content unchanged, no data loss). ANOMALY FOUND AND DISCLOSED: file 1783354873.4003086_145.hamsa,U=145:2, shows a metadata-only change -- mtime and ctime both moved from the original 2026-07-06 delivery timestamp (1783354873) to a timestamp matching this session's execution window (1783963940, ~2026-07-13 10:32 local); size and sha256 content hash are unchanged (byte-identical). No write/touch/rename command was issued against any mail file by this agent in this session (only stat, sha256sum, notmuch search/count, find, and the single sanctioned `notmuch new --no-hooks --full-scan`). No competing mbsync/notmuch/systemd-timer process was found running during the investigation window. Root cause of the single-file metadata touch is UNRESOLVED and is called out explicitly in the implementation summary as a residual anomaly for follow-up investigation -- not attributed definitively to the sanctioned remediation command, and not treated as content mutation (sha256 proves content integrity).
